sections.overview: The tuatara is the only living representative of Sphenodontia, an ancient reptile lineage once much more diverse.
sections.identification: It has a spiny crest along the back, more developed in males; despite its lizard-like shape, it is not a lizard.
sections.habitat: It lives on offshore islands in coastal forest and clearings, often where seabirds have enriched the soil.
sections.diet: It eats invertebrates and also takes lizards and other small animals when available.
sections.behavior: Adults are mainly nocturnal, though they emerge by day to bask.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in buried nests; reproduction is unusually slow for a reptile.
sections.ecology: Tuatara occur naturally only in New Zealand and are managed as one species, Sphenodon punctatus.
sections.conservation: Conservation relies on protected island populations and preventing introduced rodents from reaching them.
